verdict.rationale: The SDK documents programmatic provisioning via getSandbox(), which gets or creates a sandbox by ID. It also documents code execution with captured stdout, stderr and exit codes, plus file reads, so an agent can run the provision, execute and read loop without a human. The pack never documents an explicit teardown or destroy call, and a community member notes there is no auto-destroy after idle time, leaving cleanup to the implementer. missing for 10: a documented sandbox teardown/destroy API, an idle auto-destroy or lifecycle policy, and hands-on corroboration of a fully autonomous end-to-end agent loop.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: getSandbox() - Gets or creates a sandbox instance by ID.
sandbox.exec() - Execute shell commands in the sandbox and capture stdout, stderr, and exit codes.
Sandboxes are ideal for building AI agents that need to execute code
